runs.u: Can you recommend a messaging app?
runs.reply:
Short answer:
- Best privacy-first: Signal
- Best for reaching almost everyone: WhatsApp
- Best if you’re all on Apple devices: iMessage/FaceTime
- Best for big groups, channels, and features: Telegram (note: default chats aren’t end-to-end encrypted)
- Best open, decentralized option: Matrix (Element app)
- Best Android SMS replacement: Google Messages with RCS
- For communities/voice chat (gaming-style): Discord
- For work: Slack or Microsoft Teams

Why these picks:
- Signal: End-to-end encryption by default, minimal data collection, open source. Solid calls, groups, disappearing messages, usernames/phone number privacy. Smaller user base than WhatsApp/Telegram.
- WhatsApp: Massive network, E2EE by default, great voice/video, multi‑device works well, business features. Collects more metadata and owned by Meta.
- iMessage: Seamless on Apple devices with E2EE. Not cross‑platform; iCloud backups can weaken privacy if enabled.
- Telegram: Fast, feature-packed, huge groups, channels, bots, cloud backups. Default chats are server‑stored and not E2EE; use Secret Chats for E2EE.
- Matrix/Element: Federated and open source, E2EE, self-hosting possible. Setup and key management can be more involved; friends may not be on it.
- Google Messages (RCS): Good if you want SMS + modern chat on Android. E2EE for 1:1 and many group chats when all parties use RCS; falls back to SMS otherwise.
- Discord: Great for communities, voice channels, streaming. Not E2EE; more social than private messenger.
- Slack/Teams: Best for work with admin controls and integrations; not ideal for personal private chat.

Quick picker—tell me:
1) Your devices (iOS, Android, desktop)
2) Who you need to chat with (which apps they already use)
3) Priority: privacy or convenience/features?
4) Must-haves (group size, calls, file sharing, bots, backups, multi-device)
5) Any regional needs or access limits

Share those and I’ll recommend one app (or a combo) tailored to you.
